Abdul Matin Khasru with Habibur Rahman and Farhad Ahmed ----- For the Petitioner. 
MU Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State-Opposite Party.
parties:
Emarat Ali ------ Petitioner 
vs 
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Criminal Revision under section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of Emarat Ali is directed against the judgment and order dated 9-10-2001 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Metropolitan Criminal Appeal No, 312 of 2001 rejecting the Memo of appeal on the ground of limitation, 

 8. Thereafter, the accused petitioner preferred Criminal Appeal being No. 312 of 2001 along with a prayer for condo nation of delay of 1010 days under section 5 of the Limitation Act. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge passed the impugned judgment and order on 9-10-2001 on the point of limitation rejecting the Memo of appeal deciding that the learned Magistrate passed the judgment on 26-11-1998 and the appeal was filed on 6-9-2001 after 1010 days of passing of the judgment of the learned Magistrate; that the accused person was present during trial taking bail from the Court, he absconded himself from 13-8-1995 and that the accused person failed to explain the satisfactory grounds for condoning the delay. 

 15. Mr MU Ahmed, the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State, opposing the submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the accused petitioner failed to satisfy the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge with the grounds for condonation of delay of 1010 days in filing the appeal; that the appellate Court did not pass the judgment and order dated 9-10-2001 on merit; that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge only passed the impugned judgment and order on the point of limitation and that the judgment and order dated 9-10-2001 of learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge is quite justified which does not call for any interference. 

 16. On perusal of the record, it appears that the accused petitioner preferred this revisional application against the judgment and order dated 9-10-2001 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge in Metro Criminal Appeal No. 312 of 2001 wherein the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge disallowed the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act which was filed by petitioner along with memo of appeal and that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge was not satisfied with the grounds shown by the accused appellant for condonation of delay and that is why he rejected the memo of appeal by the impugned judgment and order dated 9-10-2001. 

 17. There is no denying of the fact that the Metropolitan Sessions Judge did not enter into the merit of the appeal arid he simply rejected the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act along with memo of appeal which speak that the Memo of appeal was not admitted for hearing. There are some stages for the disposal of a criminal case. It is admitted by all concerned that the learned Magistrate exercised his power as a trial Court and passed the judgment and order dated 26-11-1998. Thereafter, the convict petitioner preferred appeal on, 6-9-2001 with an application for condonation of delay of 1010 days but the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge before admitting the appeal took the application of delay for hearing and rejected the memo of appeal not admitting the same as he was not convinced with the grounds of delay shown by the convict appellant which induced him to pass the impugned judgment and order dated 9-10-2001. Thus it appears that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge exercised his appellate power in respect of the appeal filed by the convict appellant. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has failed to show any decision to the effect that this Division can exercise the power of appellate Court sitting as a revisional court. So, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that this Court can exercise the power of the appellate court cannot be entertained considering the facts and circumstances of the case. Because one stage of the criminal case would be usurped by this revisional Court whereby the convict appellant would be legally deprived from justice of appellate Court which will seriously cause miscarriage of justice. 

 18. Now the point for determination is, whether the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge is justified in rejecting the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act. The contention of the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act is that the petitioner was a poor driver who used to earn his livelihood by driving minibus and that he was illegally involved in this case, and thus he was financially handicapped. It is admitted that the case was started on 4-6-1993; that the charge-sheet was submitted on 20-4-1994; that the charge was framed against the accused petitioner on 8-4-1995. It appears from the order sheet of the trial Court that after framing the charge the case was adjourned time and again and the prosecution in spite of taking time repeatedly miserably failed to produce the witnesses and ultimately the trial Court passed the judgment and order of conviction on 26-11-1998. The case was started on 4-6-1993 and the learned trial Court passed the judgment on 26-11-1998 examining only informant and two investigating officers. Thus it took 5 years 5 months and 2 days. How long a poor and unemployed driver will run after a case. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the clerk of the conducting lawyer ensured him that it will take lot of time to conclude the trial and moreover, in most of the accident cases, the prosecution failed to examine the witnesses and that the accused are generally acquitted. The poor and illiterate driver like the petitioner being convinced by the assurance of the clerk of the engaged Advocate and being disgusted due to prolongation of trial went abroad for livelihood and stayed their for 5 years and after returning to Bangladesh he was arrested by the police. After his arrest his nearest relative one Abid Azad communicated with the learned Advocate and came to know that he was convicted in the aforesaid case and after collecting the certified copy of the judgment and order of the trial Court, he preferred the appeal along with an application for condonation of delay. Learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge disallowed the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, rejecting the memo of appeal by his judgment and order dated 9-10-2001. 

 24. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the main criterion for deciding in this case whether the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the accused person this such factum has not been proved by any reliable witness. Even the prosecution has not attempted to prove this important aspect of the case. In this connection, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the accused person was driving very carefully but the rickshaw puller suddenly came in front of the minibus and thus the accident was caused due to negligence of the rickshaw puller. Such submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner cannot be thrown away. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge while disposing of the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act ought to have considered all the facts and circumstances of this case but the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge did not enter into the facts and circumstances of the case and passed his judgment in a mechanical way. The impugned judgment and order dated 9-10-2001 of the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge is a non speaking order who did not consider the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 26. The pertinent question to be decided in this case is, that under what circumstances the accused petitioner did not file the appeal beyond the period of limitation. Before considering this matter, court is to consider the' fact and circumstances of this case and the law involved as stated above. 

 28. Where the court before exercising the power under section 5 of the Limitation Act, feels satisfied upon the facts of the case under consideration that the explanation given for the delay is sufficient, the discretion under section 5 of the Limitation Act should be exercised and the court should take a liberal view in considering the sufficient cause shown by the applicant. The court should not press for explanation of each hour's or each day's delay. Considering the peculiar circumstances of this case, it would be sufficient if each day's delay is not established conclusively but may satisfy the court by furnishing some general reasonable explanation. Under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the petitioner is entitled to condo nation of delay if he can satisfy the court that he had sufficient cause for not making the application within the period fixed by statute. Whether or not there was sufficient cause for not coming to court within the period prescribed by the Limitation Act is a question of fact which is to be determined keeping in view all the attending circumstances. The words 'sufficient cause' should receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice when negligence, nor inaction, nor want of bonafide is imputable to the applicant. Appellant is only required to satisfy the court that he was unable to prefer appeal in time on account of some misadventure on which it ought to have been presented beyond prescribed period and it is not necessary for him to account for inactivity during the entire period prescribed by law. 

 32. The rules of practice relating to 90 days' limitation for filing appeal not being an inflexible rule, the learned appellate Court was not justified in dismissing the appeal merely on the ground of delay without considering the merit of the case. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, if the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge could think that the appeal had merit, then he ought to have condoned the delay and admit the appeal for consideration on merit to prevent gross miscarriage of justice. 

 34. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the decision arrived at hereinbefore, the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act is considered and the delay of 1010 days in filing the criminal appeal be condoned. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge is directed to admit the appeal and to hear the appeal on the basis of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record within two months from the date of receipt of the record.
